answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work gates each new agent identity: before joining, an agent must solve a puzzle that forces heavy RAM use, not just fast cores. An honest agent pays this once, at the dawn of membership, and the cost feels as light as a zephyr. But a sybil attacker minting thousands of fake identities must repeat that expensive grind for every one, so the aggregate memory and energy bill scales linearly and soon grows as heavy as hauling marble. Faking a crowd stops being cheap.
